beliefs: Trailing whitespace is stripped (including Unicode whitespace like NBSP and em-space) [E1, E2, E5]
Leading whitespace is preserved, so '  hello' stays '  hello' and ' hello world ' stays ' hello world ' [E2, E3]
After stripping, the first character is uppercased only if it is at position 0 of the original string (no leading whitespace); if the string starts with whitespace, nothing is uppercased [E3, E7]
Uppercasing the first character uses full .upper() semantics including multi-char expansions, so 'ß'→'Ss', 'ﬁ'→'Fi', 'ﬃ'→'Ffi', 'ŉ'→'ʼN' [E6, E7, E8]
The rest of the string after the first character is left untouched, so 'straße'→'Straße' and 'ÉCOLE'→'École' [E5]
A lone space or all-space string becomes empty after trailing-strip [E1, E2]
A tab or newline at position 0 is not uppercased and is preserved, so '\thello' stays '\thello' [E2, E3]
Digits, symbols, and already-uppercase letters at position 0 are unchanged [E1, E4]
notes: Fixed the multi-char expansion: it's the full .upper() of the first char (e.g. 'ß'→'Ss', 'ﬁ'→'Fi', 'ﬃ'→'Ffi'), not just the first char of the expansion. The rest of the string is appended unchanged.
